title: Streaming: unify cancellation + disconnect semantics (AbortController parity)
author: Dana Lo
release_notes: - Streaming cancellation now consistently maps AbortController cancellation to a Redwood AbortError (code: "aborted") across Node runtimes. - Mid-stream disconnects now surface a StreamDisconnectedError and are not automatically retried; callers can opt-in to manual resume logic. - Streaming iterator now closes deterministically on abort/cancel and releases the response body reader.
body: Context: Customers (and Support) have reported inconsistent behavior when streaming responses disconnect, especially in TS apps running behind proxies or using different Node runtimes (undici vs native fetch). Today, the SDK sometimes (a) hangs until the underlying socket errors, (b) continues parsing buffered chunks after user cancellation, or (c) throws runtime-specific errors (DOMException AbortError vs undici errors), making it hard to write portable cancellation handling. This PR standardizes streaming cancellation + disconnect semantics to match the cross-SDK expectations being defined in ENG-2483 / ADR-0138. Summary of changes: 1) AbortController semantics: - If the caller aborts the request signal, streaming stops immediately, the reader is canceled, and we throw a normalized AbortError with `code="aborted"` (instead of leaking runtime-specific AbortError shapes). - If the caller aborts while waiting for the first byte (before headers), we surface the same AbortError. - If the caller aborts after some events have been yielded, the async iterator completes by throwing AbortError (consistent with Python raising CancelledError / Go context canceled semantics in our spec). 2) Disconnect handling: - If the underlying connection closes unexpectedly mid-stream (EOF / socket hangup / connection reset), we now throw StreamDisconnectedError with context: `receivedEvents`, `receivedBytes`, and (when present) `lastEventId`. - We explicitly do NOT auto-reconnect or retry mid-stream by default. This aligns with idempotency guidance: retries/resume are only safe for endpoints that support deterministic replay, which we do not guarantee today. 3) SSE frame parsing hardening: - Treat incomplete frames at end-of-stream as a disconnect error (not a silent success). - Continue to support partial chunk boundaries (data lines split across chunks). 4) Resource cleanup: - Always release the reader lock and cancel the reader on abort to avoid keeping sockets open. - Ensure the iterator terminates deterministically and does not leak pending promises. API/behavior notes: - No API surface change (same method signatures). - Error taxonomy: new `StreamDisconnectedError` and normalized `AbortError` live in `src/errors.ts` and are re-exported. - The existing `ReadableStream` adapter remains internal. Test plan: - Added regression tests that simulate: (a) abort before first chunk, (b) abort during parsing, (c) disconnect mid-event, (d) partial SSE frames across chunks, (e) undici vs native fetch error normalization via injected adapters. - Ran conformance scenarios locally for streaming cancel/disconnect (pre-harness) with mocked gateway. Related: ENG-2483 (streaming semantics), ENG-2487 (TS implementation), ENG-2489 (error taxonomy). Support signals: SUP-9321 (hang on streaming), SUP-9334 (aggressive retries are being handled separately; this PR intentionally does not add streaming retries).
commits: sdk(ts): introduce AbortError + StreamDisconnectedError with normalized codes
sdk(ts): cancel reader on abort and normalize abort/disconnect exceptions
sdk(ts): treat incomplete SSE frames on EOF as disconnect error
test(ts): add streaming cancel/disconnect coverage with injected fetch adapters
docs(ts): clarify streaming retry stance (no automatic reconnect) and cancellation handling
changed_areas: src/streaming/sse.ts (parser: incomplete frame handling, last-event-id tracking)
src/streaming/streamingClient.ts (AbortController wiring, reader cancellation, error normalization)
illustrative_snippet: New normalization helper used by the streaming iterator: `if (signal?.aborted) throw new AbortError("Request aborted", { cause: signal.reason }); try { ...read loop... } catch (err) { if (isAbortLike(err)) throw new AbortError("Request aborted", { cause: err }); if (isDisconnectLike(err)) throw new StreamDisconnectedError("Stream disconnected", { cause: err, receivedEvents, receivedBytes, lastEventId }); throw err; } finally { try { await reader.cancel(); } catch {} reader.releaseLock(); }`
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can you confirm we’re aligned with the parity spec that cancellation should throw (not silently end the iterator)? Also please add explicit notes that we don’t auto-reconnect mid-stream.

Dana Lo (author): Yep—aligned with the draft spec/ADR direction: cancellation is exceptional and should be catchable. I added a docs note + a test asserting we throw AbortError after at least one event has been yielded.

Rafael Mendes (review): Strong +1 on not auto-retrying mid-stream. One concern: make sure we always cancel the reader to avoid keeping sockets open under high churn. Also ensure abort path doesn’t trigger retry logic elsewhere.

Dana Lo (author): Added `finally` cleanup to always cancel + release the reader lock. Streaming path doesn’t pass through the retry wrapper; confirmed by tracing the call path in `client.ts` (streaming uses a distinct execution path).
Brian Murphy (review): Error taxonomy: do we have stable `code` strings for these (aborted vs stream_disconnected)? We’ll need consistency with other SDKs for docs/support.

Dana Lo (author): Added `code` fields: `aborted` and `stream_disconnected`. Also ensured message text is stable and doesn’t include runtime-specific fragments. Linked to ENG-2489 in the PR body for broader taxonomy alignment.
Elliot Price (review): Docs request: add a snippet showing AbortController usage and how to differentiate abort vs disconnect. Also mention that partial frames are treated as disconnect now.
Dana Lo (author): Added a short section to docs/streaming.md with example `try/catch` and notes about partial frames => StreamDisconnectedError.
Ibrahim Khan (follow-up): Please add one test for abort-before-headers; we’ve seen inconsistent behavior there across runtimes.
Dana Lo (author): Done—added `cancellation.abortBeforeFirstByte` test using the fake fetch adapter to delay headers until after abort.
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Approved. This matches the cross-SDK direction. Let’s make sure we call out behavior in the changelog when we roll this into the parity release.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Cleanup in finally block is important; thanks for adding it.
